info.title: Runsite Public API
info.description:
Manage Runsite projects, web services, deployments, managed databases and object storage over REST.
The same API powers the Runsite CLI and MCP server.

## Authentication

Send an API key in the `Authorization` header on every request:

```http
Authorization: Bearer ak_live_...
```

Create keys in the dashboard under **Settings → API Keys**. A missing, revoked or expired key returns `401`.

## Scopes

Each key has one scope, and each endpoint shows the minimum scope it needs.

| Scope | Allows |
|-------|--------|
| `read` | Reading projects, services, deployments, logs, metrics, buckets and storage keys |
| `write` | Everything in `read`, plus creating, deploying and changing resources, and bucket-scoped storage keys |
| `admin` | Everything in `write`, plus deleting resources and creating workspace-wide storage keys |

A key below the required scope gets `403` with
`{"code": "insufficient_scope", "required": "...", "actual": "..."}` in `detail`.

Every call also needs a workspace role: reading needs `read`, changes need `admin`.
`/api/v1` acts on the key owner's active workspace.

## Errors

Errors return a JSON body with a `detail` field. `422` means the request body or query failed validation.

## Rate limits

Limits are counted per API key. Creating projects, web services, deployments, databases and buckets is limited to
5 requests per minute; other endpoints that change state are limited to 30 requests per minute.
Over the limit you get `429`; wait and retry.

get.description: Returns the profile of the user who owns the API key. Call it to check that a key works and to see which account it acts for.
Returns the ID, name, prefix and scope of the API key sent with this request. The full key is never returned.

Lists the active plans for one `service_type`, such as `web_service`, `postgresql` or `redis`, with their resource limits and prices in cents. Pass a plan's `id` as `plan_id` when you create a web service or database.
Lists all projects in the API key owner's active workspace, with a count of services in each. The list is not paginated.

post.description: Creates an empty project in the API key owner's active workspace. Pass its `id` as `project_id` when you create web services and databases: only services in the same project can be linked with `POST /web-services/{web_service_id}/connections`.

403.description: Your workspace role does not allow creating projects.

get.description: Returns a project with the web services, PostgreSQL and Redis databases, storage buckets and email services it contains.

Lists the web services and static sites in the API key owner's active workspace, including those that are not in a project. `project_id` narrows the list to one project, or with `none` to the services outside any project. The list is not paginated.

parameters.name: project_id

schema.description: A project ID to list only that project's resources, or `none` to list only the resources outside any project. Omit it to list everything in the workspace.
schema.title: Project Id

parameters.description: A project ID to list only that project's resources, or `none` to list only the resources outside any project. Omit it to list everything in the workspace.

post.description: Creates a web service or static site from a Git repository or a container image. The service starts out `stopped` and nothing is built yet: call `POST /web-services/{web_service_id}/deployments` to build and release the first version. Variables passed in `env_vars` are saved with the service, and the service's subdomain is derived from its `name`.

400.description: The plan is invalid or not available to you, a service or instance limit is reached, the balance is too low, or no subdomain could be derived from the name.

403.description: Your workspace role does not allow creating services.

404.description: `project_id` does not match a project in your active workspace.

get.description: Returns a web service's configuration and current `status`. Poll it after a start, stop, restart or deployment to follow the transition.

post.description: Starts a stopped web service from its last built version. This is an alias of `POST /web-services/{web_service_id}/start` and does not rebuild: to build and release a new version, use `POST /web-services/{web_service_id}/deployments`.

400.description: The service has never been deployed or has no image to run, is blocked, has used up its traffic allowance, or starting it would exceed your plan's limit of active services.

409.description: The service is being deleted, or a start, stop, restart or deploy is already in progress.

503.description: The request could not be queued. Retry it.

post.description: Starts a stopped web service from its last built version, without rebuilding. The start runs in the background: the call returns `starting` right away, so poll `GET /web-services/{web_service_id}` until `status` is `running`. If the service is already running, nothing changes.

400.description: The service has never been deployed or has no image to run, is blocked, has used up its traffic allowance, or starting it would exceed your plan's limit of active services.

409.description: The service is being deleted, or a start, stop, restart or deploy is already in progress.

503.description: The request could not be queued. Retry it.

post.description: Restarts the running instances of a web service with the same image, without rebuilding. The restart runs in the background: the call returns `restarting` right away, so poll `GET /web-services/{web_service_id}` to follow it. A stopped service cannot be restarted; use `/start` instead.

400.description: The service is blocked or has used up its traffic allowance.

409.description: The service is not running, is being deleted, or another start, stop, restart or deploy is in progress.

503.description: The request could not be queued. Retry it.

post.description: Applies the service's current environment variables, project secrets and connection variables to its running instances with a rolling restart, without rebuilding. Changes made through `/env` are saved right away but reach a running service only after this call, a deploy or a start. The call returns `restarting` right away; the status then moves through `restarting` and `deploying`, so poll `GET /web-services/{web_service_id}` until it is `running` again. If the new values keep the service from becoming ready, the previous configuration is restored and the service keeps running on it; the new values stay saved, so check the logs. If the service is not running, nothing restarts: the response keeps its current `status` and says the variables will be applied the next time it starts.

400.description: The service is blocked or has used up its traffic allowance.

409.description: The service is being deleted, or a start, stop, restart or deploy is already in progress.

503.description: The request could not be queued. Retry it.

post.description: Stops all instances of a web service. Its configuration, environment variables and deployments are kept, and `/start` brings it back without rebuilding. The stop runs in the background: the call returns `stopping` right away. If the service is already stopped or sleeping, nothing changes.

409.description: The service is being deleted, or a start, stop, restart or deploy is already in progress.

503.description: The request could not be queued. Retry it.

get.description: Returns recent runtime logs of a web service as plain text. `tail` sets the number of lines (1 to 10000, default 100); `since` is a Unix timestamp in seconds that limits the output to newer lines. Static sites have no runtime logs.

400.description: The logs could not be fetched right now. Retry later.

get.description: Returns the current CPU and memory usage of a web service and the number of running instances. A service that is not running reports zeros.

Returns CPU, memory and instance count over the last `period` seconds (60 to 604800, default 3600), with points about `period / 100` seconds apart and at least 15 seconds apart. An empty `data_points` list means no metrics are available for that window.

Lists the deployments of a web service, newest first. Page through them with `limit` (1 to 100, default 10) and `offset`, which is rounded down to a multiple of `limit`; `total` counts all deployments. The deployment serving traffic has `is_live: true`. `build_logs` is always null here: read one deployment for its logs.

post.description: Builds and releases a new version of a web service from its Git repository or container image. The build runs in the background: the call returns the new deployment as `pending`, so poll `GET /web-services/{web_service_id}/deployments/{deployment_id}` until it is `running`, `failed` or `cancelled`. `branch` builds another branch for this deployment only and does not change the service's configured branch. Only one deployment can be in progress at a time.

400.description: The service has no Git repository or image, a deployment is already in progress, the service is blocked or has used up its traffic allowance, or starting it would exceed your plan's limit of active services.

get.description: Returns one deployment with its status, branch or image, and commit. Poll it after triggering a deployment or rollback to follow its progress.

404.description: Deployment not found, or it belongs to another web service.

post.description: Redeploys the image of an earlier successful deployment, without rebuilding. The call creates a new deployment that points at the target and returns it as `pending`; poll `GET /web-services/{web_service_id}/deployments/{deployment_id}` to follow it. The target must belong to this web service and have status `running`.

400.description: The target belongs to another service or did not succeed, a deployment is already in progress, or the service is blocked or has used up its traffic allowance.

404.description: Web service or target deployment not found.

get.description: Lists the environment variables of a web service. Values are always masked as `********`; the API never returns them. Variables added by `/connections`, such as `DATABASE_URL`, are included.

post.description: Adds one environment variable to a web service. Changes take effect the next time the service is started or deployed. Call `POST /web-services/{web_service_id}/apply-env` to apply them to a running service now. `APP_PORT`, `APP_NAME` and `RUNSITE_SERVICE_ID` are reserved, and `PORT` must be a number from 1 to 65535.

400.description: The key is reserved, or `PORT` is not a valid port number.

409.description: A variable with this key already exists.

put.description:
Creates, updates and deletes several environment variables of a web service in one request. Each item is handled according to its fields:

- without `id`: creates a new entry
- with `id`: replaces the key, value and flags of that entry
- with `id` and `deleted: true`: deletes that entry

Variables that are not listed stay as they are. The response lists every variable after the change, with values masked. Changes take effect the next time the service is started or deployed. Call `POST /web-services/{web_service_id}/apply-env` to apply them to a running service now.

400.description: The request repeats a key, uses a reserved key, or sets an invalid `PORT`.

404.description: Web service not found, or an `id` does not belong to this service.

409.description: A new variable uses a key that already exists.

delete.description: Deletes one environment variable from a web service. Changes take effect the next time the service is started or deployed. Call `POST /web-services/{web_service_id}/apply-env` to apply them to a running service now.

404.description: Web service or variable not found.

post.description: Gives a web service access to a PostgreSQL or Redis database in the same project by saving its connection URL as a secret environment variable: `DATABASE_URL` for `database`, `REDIS_URL` for `redis`. The URL uses the database's internal hostname. If you already set that key to another value, a numbered key such as `DATABASE_URL_2` is used instead. Changes take effect the next time the service is started or deployed.

400.description: The web service is not in a project, or the connection already exists.

403.description: Your workspace role does not allow changing this project.

404.description: Web service not found, or the target database is not in the web service's project.

get.description: Lists the secrets of a project. Values of entries with `is_secret: true` are masked as `********`; entries with `is_secret: false` are returned in plain text.

post.description: Adds a secret to a project. The value is stored encrypted and is masked in every response while `is_secret` is true.

409.description: A secret with this key already exists in the project.

put.description:
Creates, updates and deletes several secrets of a project in one request. Each item is handled according to its fields:

- without `id`: creates a new entry
- with `id`: replaces the key, value and flags of that entry
- with `id` and `deleted: true`: deletes that entry

Secrets that are not listed stay as they are. The response lists every secret of the project after the change.

400.description: Two new secrets in the request use the same key.

404.description: Project not found, or an `id` does not belong to this project.

409.description: A key is already used by another secret in the project.

delete.description: Deletes a secret from a project. This cannot be undone.

get.description: Lists the PostgreSQL and Redis databases in the API key owner's active workspace, newest first. Page through them with `limit` (1 to 100, default 50) and `offset`, which is rounded down to a multiple of `limit`. `project_id` narrows the list to one project, or with `none` to the databases outside any project. Databases being deleted are left out, and credentials are never included.

parameters.name: project_id

schema.description: A project ID to list only that project's resources, or `none` to list only the resources outside any project. Omit it to list everything in the workspace.
schema.title: Project Id

parameters.description: A project ID to list only that project's resources, or `none` to list only the resources outside any project. Omit it to list everything in the workspace.

post.description: Creates a managed PostgreSQL database. The database name, user and password are generated for you and never returned: to use the database from a web service in the same project, call `POST /web-services/{web_service_id}/connections` with `target_type: database`. Provisioning continues in the background; poll `GET /databases/{database_id}` until `status` is `running`.

400.description: The plan is invalid or not available to you, a database limit is reached, the balance is too low, or provisioning failed.

403.description: Your workspace role does not allow creating databases.

404.description: `project_id` does not match a project in your active workspace.

get.description: Returns one database with its status, plan and hostnames. For PostgreSQL it also reports current CPU and memory usage and the instance count; for Redis these fields are null. Credentials are never included.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a PostgreSQL or Redis database together with its data and backups. This cannot be undone. Once deleted, the database no longer appears in `GET /databases`.

403.description: Your workspace role does not allow deleting databases.

post.description: Creates a managed Redis database, served by Valkey. The user and password are generated for you and never returned: to use it from a web service in the same project, call `POST /web-services/{web_service_id}/connections` with `target_type: redis`. Provisioning continues in the background; poll `GET /databases/{database_id}` until `status` is `running`.

400.description: The plan is invalid or not available to you, a database limit is reached, the balance is too low, or provisioning failed.

403.description: Your workspace role does not allow creating databases.

404.description: `project_id` does not match a project in your active workspace.

post.description: Starts a stopped PostgreSQL or Redis database. The call returns `starting` right away; poll `GET /databases/{database_id}` until `status` is `running`. If the database is already running, nothing changes. A suspended database cannot be started.

400.description: The database is suspended, the balance is too low, or the start failed.

403.description: Your workspace role does not allow starting databases.

409.description: The database is still being created, started or stopped.

post.description: Stops a running PostgreSQL or Redis database. Its data and plan are kept, and `/start` brings it back. If the database is already stopped, nothing changes.

403.description: Your workspace role does not allow stopping databases.

409.description: The database is still being created, started or stopped.

get.description: Lists the object storage buckets in the API key owner's active workspace.

post.description: Creates a bucket in the active workspace. Names are 3-63 characters of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and are unique across all Runsite accounts. No access key is created; call `POST /storage/keys` to get S3 credentials, or connect the bucket to a web service in the dashboard.

403.description: Your API key scope or workspace role does not allow this action.

400.description: The name is invalid, or the workspace has reached its bucket quota.

409.description: The name is already taken, possibly by another account.

get.description: Returns one bucket with its size and object count.

patch.description: Makes a bucket public (anonymous GET of its objects) or private. `is_public` is required.

403.description: Your API key scope or workspace role does not allow this action.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a bucket and every object in it. This cannot be undone.

403.description: Your API key scope or workspace role does not allow this action.

get.description: Lists S3 access keys. Secret keys are never returned after creation.

post.description: Creates an S3 access key for one bucket (`bucket_id`, needs `write` scope) or for the whole workspace (no `bucket_id`, needs `admin` scope, because a workspace-wide key can create and delete buckets over S3). The secret key is returned only in this response. Keys can read, write and, when `delete` is set, delete objects; they never get the storage `admin` permission.

403.description: Your API key scope or workspace role does not allow this action.

delete.description: Revokes an S3 access key. Requests signed with it stop working within about 5 minutes, because storage caches recently used keys.

403.description: Your API key scope or workspace role does not allow this action.

id.title: Id
id.description: Unique identifier of the API key.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name given to the key when it was created.

key_prefix.title: Key Prefix
key_prefix.description: First 8 characters after `ak_live_`, shown to help identify the key. The full key is never returned.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Permission level of the key: `read`, `write` or `admin`. Each level includes the ones below.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When the key stops working (ISO 8601, UTC). Null if it never expires.

last_used_at.title: Last Used At
last_used_at.description: When the key last authenticated a request (ISO 8601, UTC). Null if never used.

ApiKeyIdentity.title: ApiKeyIdentity
ApiKeyIdentity.description: What the presented API key is allowed to do. Never carries the key itself.

logs.title: Logs
logs.description: Runtime log output of the service's containers as plain text, newline-separated. Static sites return an explanatory message instead, since they have no runtime logs.
examples:
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000
INFO:     Application startup complete.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: Time the logs were fetched (ISO 8601, UTC).

service_id.title: Service Id
service_id.description: Short platform identifier of the database, also used as its internal hostname.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: ID of the user who created the database.

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: Project the database belongs to; null when it is standalone.

suspended_at.title: Suspended At
suspended_at.description: When the database was suspended, ISO 8601 in UTC; null if never suspended.

trial_ends_at.title: Trial Ends At
trial_ends_at.description: When the free trial ends and the database is suspended, ISO 8601 in UTC; null for paid plans and in public API responses.

final_backup_id.title: Final Backup Id
final_backup_id.description: Backup taken at suspension and kept for 365 days; null if the database was suspended without one.

resources_reclaimed_at.title: Resources Reclaimed At
resources_reclaimed_at.description: When the suspended database's storage was released, ISO 8601 in UTC; null while it still exists.

db_name.title: Db Name
db_name.description: Name of the PostgreSQL database inside the cluster.

db_user.title: Db User
db_user.description: PostgreSQL role that owns the database.

external_port.title: External Port
external_port.description: Legacy external port; null for current instances and whenever public access is off.

internal_hostname.title: Internal Hostname
internal_hostname.description: Hostname reachable from web services inside the platform network, on port 5432.

internal_url.title: Internal Url
internal_url.description: In-cluster connection URL with credentials. Not populated by the public API, which never returns credentials; use `POST /web-services/{id}/connections` to inject it.

external_url.title: External Url
external_url.description: Public connection URL with credentials. Not populated by the public API, which never returns credentials; use `POST /web-services/{id}/connections` to inject it.

plan.description: Full service plan the database runs on; null when not loaded or not set.

memory_limit_mb.title: Memory Limit Mb
memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit in MB, taken from the plan.

storage_limit_gb.title: Storage Limit Gb
storage_limit_gb.description: Total provisioned storage in GB (plan storage plus any extra).

storage_autoscaling.title: Storage Autoscaling
storage_autoscaling.description: Whether storage autoscaling was requested at creation.

external_hostname.title: External Hostname
external_hostname.description: Public TLS hostname for connections from outside the platform; null while public access is off.

public_access_enabled.title: Public Access Enabled
public_access_enabled.description: Whether the database accepts connections from the internet.

storage_price_cents.title: Storage Price Cents
storage_price_cents.description: Monthly price of storage beyond the plan's allowance, in EUR cents; null in public API responses.

total_monthly_price_cents.title: Total Monthly Price Cents
total_monthly_price_cents.description: Plan price plus extra storage, in EUR cents per month; null in public API responses.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: Last modification time, ISO 8601 in UTC.

DatabaseStatus.title: DatabaseStatus
DatabaseStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a managed PostgreSQL database.

`creating`, `starting` and `stopping` are transitional. `suspended` follows an expired free trial or a week
stopped for non-payment; it cannot be started again, only restored from its final backup.
`pending_deletion` means deletion is in progress; `marked_for_deletion` is a legacy state no longer set.

deployments.title: Deployments
deployments.description: Deployments on this page, newest first.

total.title: Total
total.description: Total number of deployments for the web service across all pages.

web_service_id.title: Web Service Id
web_service_id.description: ID of the web service this deployment belongs to.

commit_sha.title: Commit Sha
commit_sha.description: Full Git commit SHA that was built; null for image deployments or before the source is cloned.

commit_message.title: Commit Message
commit_message.description: Message of the deployed Git commit; null when unknown.

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: Git branch that was deployed; null for services deployed from a container image.

image_ref.title: Image Ref
image_ref.description: Container image reference deployed; set only for services deployed from an image.

image_digest.title: Image Digest
image_digest.description: Resolved content digest of the deployed image; null when not resolved.

status.description: Current lifecycle status of the deployment.

is_live.title: Is Live
is_live.description: True for the one deployment currently serving traffic; older successful deployments are false.

build_logs.title: Build Logs
build_logs.description: Build and rollout log output as plain text; null until the build produces output.
examples:
Cloning repository...
Building image...
Deployment is live.

error_message.title: Error Message
error_message.description: Human-readable reason the deployment failed or was cancelled; null otherwise.
examples: Application did not start within the allowed time.

error_category.title: Error Category
error_category.description: Machine-readable failure cause, e.g. oom, missing_dependency, port_conflict, healthcheck_timeout, build_timeout or unknown; null when the deployment did not fail.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: Time the build started (ISO 8601, UTC); null while the deployment is still pending.

finished_at.title: Finished At
finished_at.description: Time the deployment reached a final status (ISO 8601, UTC); null while it is in progress.

rollback_from_deployment_id.title: Rollback From Deployment Id
rollback_from_deployment_id.description: For a manual rollback, the ID of the earlier deployment whose version is being restored.

auto_rolled_back.title: Auto Rolled Back
auto_rolled_back.description: True if this deployment failed and the platform automatically restored the previous version.

auto_rolled_back_to_deployment_id.title: Auto Rolled Back To Deployment Id
auto_rolled_back_to_deployment_id.description: ID of the deployment the platform automatically rolled back to; null if no automatic rollback.

triggered_by_user_id.title: Triggered By User Id
triggered_by_user_id.description: ID of the user who triggered the deployment; null if unknown or the user was deleted.

triggered_by_user.description: User who triggered the deployment; null if unknown or the user was deleted.

trigger_type.title: Trigger Type
trigger_type.description: How the deployment was started: manual (dashboard, API or CLI), webhook (Git push), hook (deploy hook URL) or rollback.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: Time the deployment was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

status.description: Current runtime status of the web service.

container_id.title: Container Id
container_id.description: Internal container identifier, or null when none is recorded.

host_port.title: Host Port
host_port.description: Internal host port of the service, or null when none is recorded.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the user, or null if not set.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of an existing variable to update or delete; omit to create a new variable.

key.title: Key
key.description: Variable name: uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Updating an existing variable with a different key renames it.

value.title: Value
value.description: Plain-text value, stored encrypted; required unless `deleted` is true. Always send the real value on update: the masked "********" would be saved literally.

deleted.title: Deleted
deleted.description: Set to true together with id to delete that variable.

environment_variables.title: Environment Variables
environment_variables.description: All environment variables of the web service after the update, with values masked.

total.title: Total
total.description: Number of variables the web service has after the update.

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Variables to create, update or delete, applied in one transaction. Variables not listed are left unchanged.

key.title: Key
key.description: Variable name: uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. APP_PORT, APP_NAME and RUNSITE_SERVICE_ID are reserved by the platform.

value.title: Value
value.description: Plain-text value; stored encrypted, never returned by the public API. PORT must be 1-65535.

environment_variables.title: Environment Variables
environment_variables.description: All environment variables of the web service, with values masked.

web_service_id.title: Web Service Id
web_service_id.description: ID of the web service the variable belongs to.

value.title: Value
value.description: Always the mask "********"; the public API never returns values, whether secret or not.

is_secret.title: Is Secret
is_secret.description: Whether the variable is marked as sensitive.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: Time the variable was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: Time the variable was last changed (ISO 8601, UTC).

id.title: Id
id.description: Identifier of the bucket or email service in its own service.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the bucket or email service.

status.title: Status
status.description: Status last reported by the object storage or email service.

is_public.title: Is Public
is_public.description: Whether the bucket allows public reads. Null for email services or when unknown.

sandbox_mode.title: Sandbox Mode
sandbox_mode.description: Whether the email service is in sandbox mode. Null for buckets or when unknown.

storage_bytes_used.title: Storage Bytes Used
storage_bytes_used.description: Bytes stored in the bucket, as last reported. Null for email services or when unknown.

object_count.title: Object Count
object_count.description: Number of objects in the bucket, as last reported. Null for email services or when unknown.

cpu_usage_millicores.title: Cpu Usage Millicores
cpu_usage_millicores.description: CPU used, summed across all running instances, in millicores (1000 = 1 core).

cpu_limit_millicores.title: Cpu Limit Millicores
cpu_limit_millicores.description: CPU limit summed across all running instances, in millicores (1000 = 1 core).

cpu_usage_percent.title: Cpu Usage Percent
cpu_usage_percent.description: CPU usage as a percentage of the CPU limit, rounded to two decimals.

memory_usage_bytes.title: Memory Usage Bytes
memory_usage_bytes.description: Memory working set summed across all running instances, in bytes.

memory_limit_bytes.title: Memory Limit Bytes
memory_limit_bytes.description: Memory limit summed across all running instances, in bytes.

memory_usage_percent.title: Memory Usage Percent
memory_usage_percent.description: Memory usage as a percentage of the memory limit, rounded to two decimals.

instance_count.title: Instance Count
instance_count.description: Number of running instances (pods) of the service.

data_points.title: Data Points
data_points.description: Resource samples ordered oldest first; empty when no metrics are available.

period_seconds.title: Period Seconds
period_seconds.description: Length of the returned time window in seconds, capped at 604800 (7 days).

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the project, 1 to 100 characters.

description.title: Description
description.description: Optional free-text description of the project.
examples: Storefront, API and databases for the Acme shop.

description.title: Description
description.description: Free-text description of the project. Null when not set.
examples: Storefront, API and databases for the Acme shop.

workspace_id.title: Workspace Id
workspace_id.description: Identifier of the workspace that owns the project.

service_summary.description: Count of services in the project, by service type.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: When the project was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

updated_at.title: Updated At

app__constants__deployment__DeploymentSt.title: DeploymentStatus
app__constants__deployment__DeploymentSt.description:
Lifecycle status of a deployment.

pending: queued, waiting for a build worker. cloning: fetching the repository source.
building: building the container image. deploying: rolling the new image out to the cluster.
running: completed successfully (past deployments keep this status; see is_live for the one serving traffic).
failed: build or rollout failed. rolling_back: the new version failed its checks and the previous
successful deployment is being restored. cancelled: stopped before it finished.
